title: 10 Correct Builds. 4 Shipped.
caption:
The model wrote correct code. The harness threw it away.

Greg Herlein pointed five terminal agents at one local qwen model, ten rounds each. One agent built a correct binary all ten times and finished four — the other six hit a 100-turn cap and exited with the work in the trash.

Then his own agent passed its own 25 tests and rejected nothing malformed. The tests encoded the same misreading as the code, so they agreed perfectly.

I've blamed the model for my own loop more than once. The higher-fidelity build fixed none of it: 1.7x the memory, identical bugs.

Where does your agent quit?

slides.headline:
10 Correct Builds.
4 Shipped.
slides.sub: One local model. Five coding agents. Ten rounds each.

slides.headline: The Code Was Right
slides.sub: ~0.97 median correctness on the three reliable agents. Finishing was the failure, not thinking.

slides.title: How the Runs Died
items: hax — correct binary 10 of 10. Six runs died at the 100-turn cap, work discarded.
kit — declared done after 3 turns. No tests, no Makefile, no binary.
pi — one run burned 679 turns and 85M tokens without ever stopping.

slides.title: It Passed Its Own Tests
slides.sub: 25 test functions, all green. The binary accepted bad CRCs, truncated files and zero-byte garbage.

slides.headline: Q8 Bought Nothing
slides.sub: Same weights at higher fidelity. 1.7x the memory and latency. Identical failures, and two agents got worse.

slides.title: What Actually Worked
items: A done-gate the harness runs: build and test must pass before the agent can finish.
An independent reviewer against the spec, not the agent's own tests.
At the budget cap, commit best-effort. Never bin a correct binary.

slides.headline: 90% Was the Harness
slides.sub: and I'll send the done-gate checklist
